Converts a raster to a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG): tiled, with overviews, directories before the data and lossless compression. Large GeoTIFFs are read by windows, so they don't need to fit in memory.

**Toolbox folder:** Raster Processing<br>
**Status:** Experimental<br>
**Keywords:** IO, COG, Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF, Raster, Overviews, Writing<br>
**Authors:** Andrea Antonello<br>
**Class:** `org.hortonmachine.modules.RasterToCog`

**Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inRaster` | raster file |  |  | The raster to convert. |
| `pResampling` | String |  | `auto` | How the overviews are computed from 2x2 cells: auto (average for floating point data, mode for integer data like codes or classes), average, nearest (upper left cell) or mode (most frequent value). Allowed values: `auto`, `average`, `nearest`, `mode`. |
| `pCompression` | String |  | `deflate` | The lossless compression: deflate (default) or lzw. Allowed values: `deflate`, `lzw`. |
| `pDeflateLevel` | int |  | `6` | The deflate level, from 1 (fastest) to 9 (smallest), default is 6. |
| `doPredictor` | boolean |  | `true` | Use the TIFF predictor that fits the data type (horizontal for integers, floating point for floats), usually giving smaller files (default is true). |
| `pTileSize` | int |  | `512` | The size of the tiles, a multiple of 16 (default is 512). |
| `pThreads` | int |  | number of processors | The number of threads compressing the tiles (defaults to the number of available processors). |

**Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outCog` | output file |  | The output COG file. |

**Notes**

The COG is written as the COG driver of GDAL does: square tiles, overviews halving the resolution until the image fits a single tile, all the image directories at the beginning of the file, then the tiles of the smallest overview first and those of the full resolution last. So a client reading the file over HTTP, as a web map or QGIS, gets the part and the resolution it needs with a few range requests, without downloading the file.

The compression is lossless, and the tiles are compressed in parallel. The input is read by windows when it is a GeoTIFF, and the compressed tiles go to a temporary file next to the output, so rasters larger than the memory can be converted; BigTIFF is used when the file exceeds 4 GB. The nodata of the file is the one of the input if it has one, else NaN for floating point data and the novalue of the raster for integer data.
